page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Two margin notes stand in the right margin, beside the lines "Ante omnia hic" and "mihi perinde". Running head at top left, page number at top right.

main_text.p: Deinde, quo tempore maior fit resolutio, eo maiori opus est refectione.

A tempore prandii, ob vigilias precedentes & subsequentes, resolutio fit euidentior & maior, quam tempore cœnæ. Ergo in prandio maiori opus est refectione, ante enim prandium & diu à prandio exercitiis se solent homines oblectare.

Ad extremum experientiâ, se muniunt, quæ testantur vigiliam concoctionem maturare, vigilantes enim plus cibi 8. horarum spatio conficere, & 15. vel 16. horis dormientes: adducitur quoque autoritas Plinii, qui pernigilio cibos præcipuè vinci ait. Et Hippocr. 6. Epid. vigiliam homines reddere edaces afferentis, quod motu, quo viuntur vigilantes excitetur calor & augeatur. In hac controuersia quid statuendum? Ante omnia hic Iudicij quemlibet nosse corporis sui naturam oportet: autoris mihi perinde est, sive largius cœnem sive parcius, modo bene cœnem, hoc est, citra virium corporis iacturam: prout plura pauciorumue [?] alimenta in prandio vel cœna, sive domi sim mea, sive aliena, offerantur, ita & esto, nunc in prandio largius, nunc in cœna, pro appetitu desiderio.

Ego vitius rationem eam esse optimam existimarem, quâ nec plura, nec pauciora, nec valentiora alimenta in prandio apponerentur, quàm cœna, ut ubiq; æquabilitas mereretur laudem, quæ sicut in omni vita pulchra [?] est, ita esset hic maxime. Quorsum enim quasi [?] prodest, exquisito se saginare prandio, in cœna vero ieiunare, vel

page.notes: Running head read as "PROROGANDA"; the last letters are clear enough but the word is set in spaced capitals and may differ slightly. Margin note "Iudicij" is set beside "Ante omnia hic"; the second note reads "autoris" and may be "autorise" in the scan. Doubtful words: "pauciorumue", "pulchra", "quasi", "dormientes" (printed "domientes" in the scan, likely a printer's error for dormientes). The numeral after "cibi" appears as 8. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. The phrase "Ego vitius" is as printed, probably a misprint for "Ego vero" or similar; it is left as the scan shows. The final word "vel" is the last printed line on the page.
